edges.reason: msg.sender is read and returned by _msgSender().
Ownable constructor uses _msgSender() as the initial owner identity, so the deployer-controlled address flows into _transferOwnership.
Ownable constructor calls _transferOwnership(_msgSender()) to set the initial owner.
withdraw is guarded by onlyOwner, which evaluates msg.sender against owner(); an unauthorized caller is rejected.
The onlyOwner modifier on withdraw reads the privileged state through owner().
renounceOwnership is restricted by onlyOwner using msg.sender.
transferOwnership is restricted by onlyOwner using msg.sender.
renounceOwnership authorization depends on owner() through the onlyOwner modifier.
transferOwnership authorization depends on owner() through the onlyOwner modifier.
The token state variable is the target contract of the external transfer call inside withdraw.
withdraw executes the statement token.transfer(msg.sender, amount) after the onlyOwner check.
msg.sender is passed as the recipient of the token transfer, sending withdrawn funds to the caller.
The amount parameter flows directly into token.transfer without any bound or balance validation.
The external token.transfer call happens as the last action of withdraw with no reentrancy guard and no state bookkeeping, so a malicious token can re-enter withdraw before completion.
The unsafe operation is a call into the IERC20.transfer interface function.
renounceOwnership calls the internal _transferOwnership(address(0)), permanently removing the owner.
transferOwnership calls the internal _transferOwnership(newOwner), a privileged ownership mutation.
The newOwner argument is forwarded from transferOwnership into _transferOwnership.
The internal newOwner parameter is written directly into the _owner storage slot.
_transferOwnership performs the unsafe single-step assignment _owner = newOwner.
owner() returns the value held in the _owner state variable.
The current _owner value is read and then overwritten by the ownership write operation.
_transferOwnership updates the _owner state variable to the new owner address.
The oldOwner local variable caches _owner before the ownership mutation is applied.

normalization_plan.reason: The external newOwner parameter only exists as the argument of transferOwnership and is fully consumed by that function's ownership transfer path.
The internal newOwner parameter is only used to write the _owner slot, so it collapses into the ownership-write unsafe operation.
The oldOwner local is a temporary cache of _owner used solely for the event emission inside _transferOwnership.
The amount parameter exists only to size the token.transfer call in withdraw and can be merged into that unsafe external-call operation.
